questions: Does oval progress rise above about 0.4 compared with the 60 mm span at 12 mm footprint (0.275)? If it reaches about 0.66, the span is the controlling variable and 40 mm is the base for the next iteration.
Do line_loss_events stay near 1 to 1.4 on all three tracks with the 50 mm span? If they rise above about 1.5, the outer sensors are losing the tape at this span.
What kp, ki and kd did you use for the 50 mm span, and did you scale kp relative to the 60 mm span (kp 6)? Did steering_oscillation stay near 0.2 to 0.3?
Do max_error excursions (about 0.063 to 0.065 m) still happen at the same bend locations, and do they start before or after a line-loss event?
If progress recovers but max_error stays at 0.062 to 0.065 m, would you accept wheel_track 0.10 in the next iteration, with no other geometry change?

intent: Narrow the sensor span from 60 mm to 50 mm (x = -0.025, -0.0125, 0, 0.0125, 0.025) and keep the 12 mm footprint and y = 0.05 lead, so that span is the only geometry variable changed. This tests whether the progress drop seen at 60 mm is caused by span. Expected: oval progress rises from 0.275 toward 0.4 to 0.6, line-loss events stay near 1 to 1.4, and max_error stays near 0.06 to 0.065 m.
learning: Iterations 0 and 3 share footprint (12 mm) and lead (y 0.05) and differ only in span (40 mm vs 60 mm): oval progress 0.664 vs 0.275. This is the strongest contrast so far, and it points at span. Iteration 2 with 16 mm footprints at 60 mm reached 0.405, so footprint size also matters at this span. The 50 mm test sits between these points and will show whether progress is monotonic in span.
rationale: Evidence across four iterations. Iteration 0 (40 mm span, 12 mm footprint, y 0.05) is the only design that finished a run and has the best oval progress (0.664) and best score (159.7). Iteration 2 (60 mm span, 16 mm, y 0.05) reached oval progress 0.405 and score 133.7. Iteration 3 changed only the footprint, from 16 mm to 12 mm, at the 60 mm span. Oval progress fell to 0.275 and the score fell to 112.9. So the footprint is not the limit: the 12 mm footprint is worse at 60 mm, and the 16 mm footprint was better. Iteration 1 showed that the shorter lead (y 0.03) collapses progress, so the lead stays at 0.05. max_error sits at 0.062 to 0.065 m in every iteration, which is just over the 0.06 m off-track limit, and it does not respond to span, footprint or lead. Taken together, progress tracks the span: 40 mm gives 0.664 with 12 mm footprints, while 60 mm gives 0.275 with 12 mm and 0.405 with 16 mm. The Integrator's rule (oval progress at or below 0.4 with the footprint already at 12 mm means narrow the span) applies. I narrow the span from 60 mm to 50 mm, keep the 12 mm footprint and y 0.05, and change nothing else. This sits between the 40 mm point that gave the best progress and the 60 mm point that gave the worst, so it tests whether progress recovers as the span narrows. I expect oval progress between 0.4 and 0.6 and line-loss events near 1 to 1.4. If progress reaches about 0.66 again, the span is the controlling variable and 40 mm should be the base for the next iteration. If progress stays below about 0.4, the span is not the whole story and the next lever is wheel_track 0.10 for max_error. Body, wheel and mass stay unchanged so the sensing span is the only geometry variable.
